sections.html:
Lafayette is a home rule city in southeastern Boulder County, between Boulder and Denver. The 2020 census counted 30,411 residents in 12,070 households, and only 3.1 percent of the 12,456 housing units sat vacant. With so few empty homes, sellers are not up against a glut of vacant listings, though a house that needs work still has to be priced for its condition.

The city touches Erie, Broomfield and Louisville, so a Lafayette mailing address can sit in a different jurisdiction than you expect. Check your address against city limits before assuming which rules apply. Its position between Boulder, Longmont and Broomfield means a house here can draw interest from several directions.

Housing varies by decade. Houses near the original 1888 plat in Old Town may be much older than those in newer subdivisions, and buyers' repair questions will differ to match. The population grew from 8,985 in 1980 to 30,411 in 2020, which explains the long span of construction years across town.

sections.h2: Boulder County property tax due dates
sections.html:
Payment optionDue date
First halfLate February or the first business day of March
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Colorado lets you pay everything at once or in two equal installments. Boulder County gives no discount for paying early. A first-half payment made in March carries 1 percent interest, and the rate climbs to 6 percent by August. On a mailed payment, the postmark date counts as the payment date. Send checks to the Boulder County Treasurer, and never mail cash. Call the treasurer for the exact first-half date this year.

The Treasurer's office is in Boulder at 1325 Pearl Street. The county's Lafayette location at 1755 S. Public Road is closed until late January 2027.

When a house sells mid-year, the closing company prorates the tax bill between you and the buyer. Ask your title officer how that will be handled before you sign, and ask what the parcel currently owes so nothing surprises you on the closing statement.

Boulder Valley School District serves Lafayette. Families moving in often start with school boundaries, so telling a buyer which district covers the address saves them a step. Boundaries change, so confirm assignments with the district and not with an old listing.

sections.h2: Selling to a cash buyer in Lafayette
sections.html:
Dropping the loan and appraisal steps means the closing date depends mostly on title work and your schedule. A title company handles the transfer, and the deed is recorded through the Boulder County Clerk and Recorder.

  • You tell us about the house, its condition and any tenants.
  • If you accept the offer, the title company prepares the closing documents and the tax proration.
  • You pick a closing date that fits your move.

We buy houses as they are. You do not need to paint, replace flooring or clear out the garage. An as-is sale suits inherited houses, houses with tenants, and houses where the repair estimate is more than the owner wants to spend.

A house that sits unfinished through repairs still costs its owner taxes, utilities and insurance every month. Before you commit to fixing a house for a listing, add up those months and the repair bills, then compare the total with a cash offer made on the house as it stands. For some owners the gap is small. For others a quick sale is plainly cheaper.

sections.h2: What Lafayette sellers usually run into
sections.html:
Timing, condition and carrying costs top the list. Each is easier to manage once you know your options.

  • A job change that moves you out of the Boulder and Denver corridor.
  • An older Old Town house with updates you cannot afford.
  • A property inherited from a relative who lived in Lafayette for decades.
  • A rental you no longer want to manage.

If one of these fits, send us the address. Asking costs nothing, and you decide whether to go ahead.

Gather the most recent Boulder County tax statement, the mortgage servicer's contact information if a loan remains, and a note on any repairs you know about. If tenants live there, have the lease handy. If the house came to you through an estate, confirm who has authority to sign. None of this has to be perfect. The title company fills in the rest during its search.

At closing, the title company reviews the final figures with you, deducts taxes and any loan balance, and pays out the remainder after the deed is recorded.

Old Town centers on Public Road and Chester Street, with newer townhomes standing beside historic commercial buildings on Simpson Street. The town began in 1888, and coal mining shaped its early decades, so some close-in houses are very old. Expect questions about wiring, plumbing, foundations and sewer lines on those properties. You can answer by sharing whatever work has been done and when. A buyer who purchases for cash simply prices the unknowns, so you are not asked to hire inspectors or contractors to prove the house is sound.

Heirs often inherit a house in a town they no longer live in. Start by confirming who is legally able to sign. Then gather the deed, the latest tax statement and a list of anything still owed. The title company handles the search, and the deed is recorded with the Boulder County Clerk and Recorder after you sign. If relatives live in different states, a single closing date and electronic paperwork can spare everyone months of upkeep.

Meanwhile, the house keeps generating bills. Utilities, insurance and the next tax installment all keep coming, and an empty house needs checking on. That is a real reason to decide sooner than later.

If you are done managing a rental, you can sell with tenants in place or after they leave. Tell the buyer the lease terms and rent, and say whether the tenants intend to stay. A buyer who keeps them inherits the lease, so be accurate about what it says. If the unit is vacant, mention how long and what condition it is in. Either way, the process matches a standard sale: offer, title work, signing and recording.

The buyer looks at the address, the condition of the roof, systems and finishes, and any tenants or title questions. A short visit usually follows. Then you receive a number. If it works, the title company opens the file, and if it does not, you owe nothing and can ask again later or list the house the traditional way. The point of the process is that you see the number before you commit to anything.

faqs.q: What county is Lafayette, CO in?
faqs.a: Southeastern Boulder County. Property tax is billed by the Boulder County Treasurer, and deeds are recorded with the Boulder County Clerk and Recorder.

faqs.q: When are Lafayette property taxes due?
faqs.a: Boulder County offers two half payments, with the second due June 15, or one full payment due April 30. Call the treasurer for the first-half date, since it shifts when the end of February falls on a weekend.
Boulder Valley School District. Centaurus High School and Angevine Middle School are the main public secondary schools, and Peak to Peak Charter School offers kindergarten through high school.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lafayette house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so you do not have to repair, paint or clean before closing. The offer reflects the condition.

faqs.q: Does Boulder County give a discount for paying property tax early?
faqs.a: No. A first-half payment made in March carries 1 percent interest, which climbs to 6 percent by August.
